transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I came in because I just can't shake this certainty that I'm being punished for letting my father decline. My sister keeps trying to reason with me... she shows me the doctor's notes and tells me I've done everything right. But it doesn't change anything. It just feels like some kind of judgment has already been passed on me, and I don't know how to get past it.
Alongside these feelings of guilt, have you been feeling persistently down or depressed?

Yes, I have. Most days I wake up with this heavy, hollow feeling. It's almost like the color has just gone out of everything. I can sit at my desk at work—I'm in HR—or I'll just be staring at the garden beds at home, and it just feels like none of it reaches me anymore.
Have you ever experienced these feelings of being judged or punished at times when you were not feeling depressed?

No, I haven't. I never heard voices or... or believed I was being punished before this whole heavy feeling settled in. None of that happened before my father's decline. For months I was just feeling really low, and guilty, and just completely worn down. It was only after all those months of feeling like that... that's when these experiences of being judged and punished actually started.
Have you ever experienced a period of feeling this depressed earlier in your life, before this current episode began?

No, I haven't. I mean, I've had stressful periods in my life before, just normal things, but... never anything like this. I've never felt this completely down or empty before all of this started with my dad. This is really the first time I've ever dealt with something this heavy.
